solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Where to see Etonians gain military award, right? (7)

blocks.note: DSO = Distinguished Service Order, a British military decoration

annotation.surface: A question about spotting old Etonians who have picked up medals for bravery.
annotation.walkthrough: Eton College stands just across the Thames from Windsor, so that is where you see Etonians.
annotation.definitionFit: Eton sits beside Windsor, so Windsor is the place to see its pupils.

clue.text: Condiment is no longer somewhat timeless (6)

indicators.note: timeLESS: the T is taken away from A BIT

blocks.note: somewhat = A BIT; without its T (time) it is A BI

annotation.surface: A wistful remark that a condiment has lost its timeless quality.
annotation.walkthrough: Timeless is split in two: T is time, and 'less' removes it from A BIT.
annotation.definitionFit: Wasabi is the hot green Japanese paste served with sushi.

clue.text: Return of police force? A day is not settled (7)

indicators.note: a return sends the pieces back the other way

annotation.surface: Someone wonders whether the police force will come back, as nothing has been settled.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole string CID + A + MON is read backwards, not just the police force.
annotation.definitionFit: Nomadic people move about rather than settling in one place.

clue.text: American’s knockout has failed, punching morose drunk (9)

indicators.note: HAS breaks down into a new order
a punch goes into its target
MOROSE staggers into a new order

blocks.note: first part of MOROSE rearranged as SMEROO
HAS rearranged, punched into the middle

annotation.surface: A gloomy drunk takes a swing and misses, in the language of a boxing report.
annotation.walkthrough: Knockout here means a stunning success, not a punch; smasheroo is American slang for a smash hit.
annotation.definitionFit: A knockout is a sensation, which is what a smasheroo is in American slang.

clue.text: Are you texting personnel in mining area? (4)

indicators.note: text-speak writes 'are you' as R U

blocks.note: R U = are you in a text message
HR = human resources, the personnel department

annotation.surface: Someone texts to ask whether you are working in HR at a mine.
annotation.walkthrough: The Ruhr is Germany's great coal-mining and industrial valley.
annotation.definitionFit: The Ruhr valley was famous for its coal mines.

clue.text: Giving a wave to page, monarch and imperial family (7)

annotation.surface: Royals waving to a page, as at a court ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: The royal wave is a false trail: the wave is put into hair.
annotation.definitionFit: A hairdresser's perm sets curls or waves into straight hair, so the wave is a hairstyle, not a gesture.

clue.text: Following delivery job with role outside in uniform (10)

indicators.note: take the outside letters of the word that follows

annotation.surface: A delivery driver takes a job that means wearing a uniform.
annotation.walkthrough: Delivery here is childbirth, not parcels.
annotation.definitionFit: Postpartum means after giving birth.

clue.text: Rolls filled by kiddies regularly for traveller (5)

indicators.note: a thing filled by something has that something put inside it, so RR takes letters into its middle
at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

blocks.note: first letter of RR, the Rolls-Royce badge
last letter of RR, the Rolls-Royce badge

annotation.surface: Bread rolls stuffed by children, packed for someone on a journey.
annotation.walkthrough: Rolls is the car, abbreviated RR, not bread.
annotation.definitionFit: A rider is anyone travelling on a horse, bike or bus, so a traveller in the broad sense.

clue.text: Individually specify setter on cryptic Times puzzle finally (7)

indicators.note: TIMES is made obscure, so rearranged
at the end, so the last letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the setter speaks of themself as I

annotation.surface: A setter listing exactly what went into a cryptic Times puzzle.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about this very crossword, which hides that 'setter' just means I.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to specify things individually is to list them item by item.

clue.text: General meaning to keep artillerymen back, and a good mechanic (8)

indicators.note: GIST holds the other pieces inside
going back means travelling the wrong way, so RA reads right to left

blocks.note: start of GIST, the general meaning

annotation.surface: An army general wants to hold his gunners back, and also a decent mechanic.
annotation.walkthrough: General is not an officer: 'general meaning' is the gist. 'A good' belongs to the wordplay, leaving 'mechanic' as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A garagist runs or works in a garage, repairing cars.

clue.text: Experienced fellow feeling stymied has cracked, admitting pressure (11)

indicators.note: the letters break and re-form
to admit is to let in, so the mix takes P in with it

blocks.note: p = pressure, added to the fodder

annotation.surface: A frustrated man cracks under pressure.
annotation.walkthrough: Fellow feeling is a phrase for sympathy, not a man's emotions.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'fellow feeling' is an old phrase for sympathy, so experiencing it is a verb for sympathy.

clue.text: Some corn whiskey dropped by Don (3)

indicators.note: something dropped is let fall, so the W falls out of the word for Don

blocks.note: to don = to wear, as clothes
W is whiskey in the phonetic alphabet; this letter is dropped

annotation.surface: Some corn whiskey gets spilled by a man called Don.
annotation.walkthrough: Don is the verb 'put on', not a name; WEAR loses its W to leave EAR.
annotation.definitionFit: A cereal-farming term: an ear is the grain-bearing head of the corn plant.

clue.text: Eastern ascetic from China curtailed expression of triumph (6)

indicators.note: its tail, the last letter, is cut off

blocks.note: china = mate = BUDDY, minus its last letter
Ha! as a cry of triumph

annotation.surface: A holy man from China crying out in victory.
annotation.walkthrough: China means mate, from rhyming slang 'china plate'; the country is a false trail.
annotation.definitionFit: The Buddha renounced worldly comfort and lived as an ascetic in India.

clue.text: What choirs do, covering eg Scarborough Fair (8)

indicators.note: SING is wrapped around PORT

blocks.note: Scarborough is a Yorkshire seaside port

annotation.surface: Choirs singing the folk song Scarborough Fair.
annotation.walkthrough: The song title splits in two: Scarborough is an example of a port, and Fair is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in its games sense: playing fair is being sporting towards an opponent.

clue.text: Capers perhaps in creamy dish, in book put on line (10)

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another is inside it, so FOOL goes within TOME
in a down clue TOME with FOOL is placed on top of RY

blocks.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit and cream

annotation.surface: A recipe noting capers go into a creamy dish.
annotation.walkthrough: Capers are pranks, not the pickled buds a recipe suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: Capers, silly pranks, are an example of tomfoolery.

clue.text: Drinkers seizing last of beer obtained capacious bags (5,8)

indicators.note: CAROUSERS grabs the other letters inside
the last of a thing is its end, so the final letter of beer

annotation.surface: Drinkers grabbing the dregs of the beer and walking off with big bags.
annotation.walkthrough: Bags is old slang for trousers, so the capacious bags are baggy trousers with big pockets.
annotation.definitionFit: Cargo trousers are loose with large pockets, and bags means trousers.

clue.text: Say Mark is with East German Max (9)

blocks.note: m = mark, the old German currency

annotation.surface: Introducing a man named Mark who is with an East German called Max.
annotation.walkthrough: Max is not a name but short for maximum, an adjective here.
annotation.definitionFit: Max as in 'to the max' means the uttermost, the furthest extent.

clue.text: Showing versatility, fitting into a seedy establishment (8)

indicators.note: fitting into something means going inside it, so APT goes within A DIVE

blocks.note: start of A DIVE, a seedy bar

annotation.surface: Someone adapts well by fitting in at a dodgy bar.
annotation.walkthrough: A dive is a disreputable bar or club.
annotation.definitionFit: Being adaptive means adjusting readily, which shows versatility.

clue.text: Damned academic’s way to make two lots of us fat? (6,7)

definitions.text: Damned academic’s way to make two lots of us fat?

blocks.note: Marlowe's scholar who sold his soul to the devil

blocks.clueFragment: way to make two lots of us fat?
blocks.note: read the answer as an instruction: 'doctor' means rearrange, and the letters of the surname rearrange into US + US + FAT

annotation.surface: A worry that some damned professor's methods will fatten the two of us.
annotation.walkthrough: This works backwards: the answer read as an anagram instruction, doctor FAUSTUS, produces US US FAT.
annotation.definitionFit: Doctor Faustus, in Marlowe's play, is a scholar damned for his pact with the devil.

clue.text: Division of a real firm accepting case of evasion over raised tax (7)

indicators.note: CO takes the other letters inside
the outer letters, like a case
in a down clue VAT is written upwards

annotation.surface: A department of a genuine company caught dodging tax.
annotation.walkthrough: The real is Brazil's currency, not an adjective; 'over' just puts EN above TAV.
annotation.definitionFit: A currency fraction: the Brazilian real is split into a hundred centavos, so each is a division of it.

clue.text: Doubting Thomas Cook’s opening putrid stores (7)

indicators.note: the opening of a word is where it starts, so its first letter
to store something is to keep it inside, so SEPTIC holds C

annotation.surface: Holidaymakers doubt Thomas Cook after its new branch smells off.
annotation.walkthrough: Thomas Cook was a British travel agency, but here Doubting Thomas is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A doubting Thomas refuses to believe without proof, like the apostle.

clue.text: Ruddy duck free to shelter under fantail’s wings (6)

indicators.note: the outer letters of fantail
in a down clue O + RID sits below FL

blocks.note: a duck is a zero score in cricket

annotation.surface: A ruddy duck, a real species, finds shelter beneath a fantail pigeon's wings.
annotation.walkthrough: Ruddy duck is a bird name, but ruddy alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A florid complexion is ruddy, flushed red.

clue.text: God accordingly defends old temple (8)

indicators.note: to defend is to guard from all sides, so THEN surrounds O

blocks.note: Pan, the Greek god of the wild

annotation.surface: A god loyally guards his ancient temple.
annotation.walkthrough: Accordingly means 'so' or 'then', as in 'if so, then...'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Pantheon in Rome is the best-known ancient temple, built for all the gods.

clue.text: Big beast in fashion work turned up (5)

indicators.note: in a down clue OP reads upwards

annotation.surface: A huge animal appears in a fashion show.
annotation.walkthrough: OP is short for opus, a numbered musical work.
annotation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is among the largest land animals.

clue.text: Blair, when writing, wore out Liberals (6)

indicators.note: worn out means broken down, so WORE loses its shape and its letters re-form

annotation.surface: Tony Blair's memoirs exhaust the Liberals.
annotation.walkthrough: The Blair is Eric Blair, who wrote as George Orwell, not the prime minister.
annotation.definitionFit: Eric Blair published under the pen name George Orwell.

clue.text: The Four Tops in concert are gladly extemporising a set of bars (4)

indicators.note: take the tops, the first letters, of the next four words

blocks.note: first letters of Concert Are Gladly Extemporising

annotation.surface: The Motown group the Four Tops happily improvise a few bars on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: The Four Tops were an American soul group; here they tell you to take four initial letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A cage is built from a grid of metal bars, so the musical bars of the surface become iron ones.

clue.text: Princess in an opera, not a princess in an operetta (3)

indicators.note: 'not' excludes what follows, so the letter A is removed

annotation.surface: A trivia line contrasting an opera princess with an operetta one.
annotation.walkthrough: Aida is Verdi's princess; Princess Ida is the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta. The repeated 'princess' is deliberate.
annotation.definitionFit: Ida is the title princess of Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida.

clue.text: Ale bottles on part of sink in standard sizes (4-1-6)

indicators.note: PORTER holds the other letters inside

blocks.note: start of PORTER, a dark ale
a tap is part of a sink

annotation.surface: Beer bottles standing on the draining board.
annotation.walkthrough: Pret-a-porter is fashion's French term for ready-to-wear clothes.
annotation.definitionFit: A fashion-trade term: ready-to-wear clothes are sold off the peg in set sizes rather than made to measure.

clue.text: City with zero money deserted by one banking on thrift (7)

indicators.note: someone deserted is left behind, so MONEY is left once ONE walks out of it
banks line a river on both sides, so the wordplay's letters flank ON

blocks.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
ON as printed, banked between EC and O
MONEY with ONE taken from its middle

annotation.surface: A city loses its money when someone who was counting on thrift leaves.
annotation.walkthrough: The ONE removed is literally the letters O, N, E in the middle of M-ONE-Y.
annotation.definitionFit: Economy means thrift, careful spending.

clue.text: Were attractive books bound by European and decorated? (7)

definitions.note: ENTICED is transitive (drew in); 'were attractive' is intransitive, a loose fit

indicators.note: something bound is tied up on both sides, so E and ICED enclose NT

blocks.note: NT = New Testament, a set of books
a cake is decorated by icing

annotation.surface: A question whether European-bound, decorated books looked appealing.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: enticed normally needs an object.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: to entice is to lure, so things that enticed exerted an attraction.
